rv.q: So, all in all, a most intriguing (and, trust me, moving ) work in progress from one of Chicago's most gifted artists, put on by a generous creative ensemble that did everything in its considerable power to bring her vision to life.
It is a brave and beautiful story of a family and allows us to see the conflicts from a specific perspective.

Sadieh Rifai's playwriting debut, The Cave (based in part on her own family's story), is arguably a little overstuffed at two-and-a-half hours. But this portrait of a Palestinian American family in Ohio at the time of the first Gulf war has so many moments of pure honesty, humor, pain, and revelation that I scarcely minded.
Overall, Rifai is a playwright to watch and this is a play worth seeing.
Although Rifai had a lot to say in THE CAVE, it was hard to hear in all the noise.
H. Adoni Esho, in a touching performance, stars in “The Cave”, an extremely timely and well-acted story...

cn.t: Rifai's timely debut about a Palestinian-American family during the Gulf War runs long at 2.5 hours but delivers honest, relatable storytelling anchored by strong ensemble work and Esho's touching lead performance.
